convertibility_reason: Uses a simple perceptron neural network with built-in price data (no external indicators), straightforward entry/exit with fixed SL/TP, fixed lot sizing, no external .mqh dependencies for trading logic

derived_values.name: Perceptron weighted sum (w0 + w1*x1 + w2*x2 + w3*x3 + w4*x4)
x1: normalized price difference (Close[1]-Open[1]) scaled by Point
x2: normalized price difference (Open[1]-Close[2]) scaled by Point
x3: normalized 2-bar momentum (Close[1]-Close[3]) scaled by Point
x4: normalized 3-bar momentum (Close[1]-Open[4]) scaled by Point
Weight optimization via delta-bar-heuristic
derived_values.used_by: On-line perceptron weight update after trade close

other_exits: SL/TP hit closes position; no other explicit exit logic

custom_logic_notes: This EA uses a single-layer perceptron (neural network) with 4 inputs derived from normalized price differences over recent bars. The perceptron computes a weighted sum and enters long if output > 0, short if output < 0. Weights are updated online using a delta-bar-heuristic (Hebbian learning rule) when a trade closes: w[i] += delta * error * x[i], where error is the realized profit/loss normalized by Point, and delta is a learning rate parameter. This makes it an adaptive/learning EA rather than a fixed-rule system. The default SL and TP are both 100 pips; the StopLevel and TakeLevel inputs control these. The perceptron inputs use previous bar values ([1],[2],[3],[4]) not current bar, and the signal is evaluated once per new bar. Weight initialization is from input parameters w0-w4 (default 0.2, 0, 0, 0, 0).
python_conversion_notes: The perceptron is straightforward to implement in Python. Key considerations: (1) The 4 input features are simple normalized price differences using Close/Open values at lagged bar indices - easy to compute from OHLC data. (2) The online weight update (delta-bar-heuristic) must be applied after each trade close, using the trade's realized P/L as the error signal. (3) Since the EA only trades on new bars, bar-level data suffices for backtesting - tick data not required. (4) The weight persistence across trades means the EA state (w0-w4) must be carried forward between trade evaluations - this is sequential state that cannot be parallelized. (5) SL/TP are fixed pip values, easily modeled. (6) No external indicators needed - all inputs are raw OHLC. (7) The position gate ensures max 1 position at a time, simplifying position tracking.
